#!/bin/sh
# Fake $EDITOR for the app.editor.external (Ctrl+G) scenario.
#
# pi-rust hands the editor one argument: the path of its temp
# `prompt.md` draft (crates/pi-coding-agent/src/external_editor.rs). The
# sleep is deliberate — it keeps the normal screen (with the launch banner)
# up long enough for panel 2 to capture it before panel 3 sees the repaint.
sleep 1.2
printf 'EDITED BY EXTERNAL EDITOR #1\nsecond line\n' > "$1"

notes: A/B for app.editor.external, the chord LUM-1308 wired: the draft is typed, Ctrl+G hands the terminal to $EDITOR, and the editor's contents come back into the composer.
panel 2: 0.5s into a 1.2s editor run — the app has left the alternate screen and printed its banner, which is what the user sees while the editor owns the tty.
panel 3: after the editor exits, the app re-enters the alternate screen and the composer holds the editor's file contents, not the typed draft.
Same binary and HOME as the other LUM-1308 captures.
caption: LUM-1308 — Ctrl+G (app.editor.external) end to end in a real PTY: draft → $EDITOR → draft replaced. Panels 2-3 are two moments of one run.

panels.label: 2. Ctrl+G → the tty is handed to $EDITOR (normal screen, banner up)
expect: Pi will resume when the editor exits.

panels.label: 3. editor exited 0 → composer holds the edited file
excludes: original draft typed by the user
